iosRule: Settings/SettingsView.swift importFont: "if let reason = KudosBackupContents.fontRejectionReason(fileName:data:)" then "if let reason = fontTotalRejectionReason(adding: data.count)" both run before data.write. Services/KudosBackup.swift:33-34 maxFontEntryBytes = 4 MB, maxTotalFontBytes = 32 MB; fontRejectionReason (:52) rejects non-ttf/otf, "data.count <= maxFontEntryBytes", and "CGFont(provider) != nil". Message: "Keeping it would stop your library backup from restoring."
androidNow: files/CustomFontRepository.kt importFont checks only "if (bytes.isEmpty())" and resolveExtension (ttf/otf), then fontFileStore.writeFont. Settings › Font (settings/SettingsPages2.kt ~526-560) reads the whole stream with readBytes() and calls importFont, with no size, total or validity check. Export: BackupRepository reads every font with readFont (no cap). backup/BackupExporter.kt font loop then does "if (bytes.size > MAX_FONT_ENTRY_BYTES) throw BackupError.EntryTooLarge(path)" and "throw BackupError.InvalidPackage(\"Total font size exceeds limit\")", so after one oversized font is installed, every library backup export fails. BackupFontValidator (BackupImporter.kt:257) does the size, total and magic-byte checks, but only on import or restore.
fix: In CustomFontRepository.importFont, before writeFont: (1) run BackupFontValidator.validate(mapOf(fileName to bytes)) (it is internal in the same module and covers the 4 MB limit, the extension and the SFNT magic/loadability check), catching BackupError and returning Result.failure with iOS's wording ("…Keeping it would stop your library backup from restoring."); (2) add up the installed font sizes (listImported() + Files.size(fontPath)) and reject if that total plus bytes.size is over BackupLimits.MAX_TOTAL_FONT_BYTES, using iOS's "go over the 32 MB a backup can carry" message. No UI change is needed: SettingsPages2 already shows failure messages. Add one unit test in CustomFontRepository tests for the >4 MB and total-limit cases.
notes: I checked this in today's tree. DECISIONS.md 2026-10-04 covers only sync skipping over-limit fonts. Nothing there records a choice to skip the check when a font is installed. Fonts that are already installed and over the limit will still block export; a separate follow-up could skip them at export, but iOS doesn't do that either. I did not check whether the safety backup before Replace goes through the same exportV2 path; that's likely, but I didn't verify it.
